It should be noted that to a large degree these remarks are concerned with the application of the section 203(b)(8) exemption to bus operations. Furthermore, the contention that these remarks evidence Congress' intent to limit absolutely the exemption to "intramunicipal or occasional" operations is contradicted by the plain terms of the statute. The Senator's comments contain references to commercial zones, but nowhere are the geographic bounds of such areas prescribed. In view of the paucity and non-definitive nature of this legislative history, we do not regard it as demonstrating a congressional construction of the geographic limits of the statutory exemption provided in section 203 (b)(8). Rather, we feel that the absence of a specific definition of commercial zones indicates that it is our duty to frame a workable delimitation by examining the words of the statute in light of contemporary economic reality and modern transportation needs. This duty is mandated by section 204(a)(6) of the Act. We are also guided in this view by the pronouncements of the three-judge court reviewing the Forwarder Terminal Areas case, supra.
